Title: RC CIRCUIT TRANSIENT TROUBLESHOOTING PRACTICE II
RC CIRCUIT TRANSIENT TROUBLESHOOTING PRACTICE II
1. RC Circuit Transient Troubleshooting Practice II
w Determine the faulty component in a faulted RC transient circuit.
w Identify faulty RC transient circuits.
. The experiment in this lesson is not setup to use the selected trainer.
In this lesson, you will determine if an RC transient circuit is faulted and if so, what the fault is.
The oscilloscope is used to determine if the circuit is operating correctly by observing the waveform across the capacitor.
The waveform measurement will indicate several probable faults such as an open capacitor or a shorted resistor.
In some cases, resistance measurements are necessary to determine the faulty component.
Let's begin the lesson on RC CIRCUIT TRANSIENT TROUBLESHOOTING PRACTICE II..
. The experiment in this lesson is not setup to use the selected trainer.
The purpose of this experiment is to give you practice in determining if an RC transient circuit is operating normally and if not, to determine the faulty component.
Pick up the PC130-14B card. This card is used to practice troubleshooting RC circuit transients.
Compare the card with the schematic shown.
Notice that there are four series RC circuits on the card with different RC time constants.
Circuit D will not be used in this troubleshooting practice. Let's set up the card before we begin troubleshooting.

2. Carefully plug PC130-14B into the Test Console PC3 position.
3. Set switches S1, S2, and S3 on PC130-14B to In (right).
4. Set switch S4 on PC130-14B to Out (left).
SWITCH POSITIONS - Place S1, S2, and S3 to IN (right).
5. Set up the function generator to produce a 10 kHz square wave output. Be sure all attenuation and modulation controls are off.
6. Connect a BNC cable from the main output on the function generator to the PC2 output BNC on the Test Console.5

The experiment is now set up. Let's verify correct operation of all circuits before beginning any troubleshooting.
The 10 kHz square wave applied to circuit A exactly charges and discharges the capacitor.

If any of the waveforms are incorrect, there may be a problem with the card or your set up. Ensure your set up is correct and that you are using the oscilloscope correctly. Then check with your instructor...

The computer may now insert a fault into one of the circuits. Set the function generator to the frequency that allows for complete charge and discharge. Use the oscilloscope to determine which circuit, if any, is faulted. Then, if necessary, use a multimeter to determine the faulty component...
1. Set the input signal to the frequency that allows the capacitor in each circuit (A, B, & C) to charge and discharge and measure the waveform across the capacitor one at a time.
Are all the circuits operating normally???????
There is a fault in one of the RC transient circuits. You should not measure correct waveforms across each capacitor. Check the circuits again.
INPUT FREQUENCY - The input frequency to each circuit allows the capacitor to exactly charge and discharge (10 time constants). This is determined by the RC time constant.
Which circuit is not functioning correctly?
Measure the waveform across C1 in circuit A again with the appropriate input frequency. Notice it is correct.
Measure the waveform across C2 in circuit B again with the appropriate input frequency. Notice it is correct.
Using the waveform measured across C3, what are the probable faults?
R3 shorted is a possible fault, but if C3 is shorted, there is no signal across it. Notice the waveform you measured.
If C3 is shorted or R3 is open, there is no signal across the capacitor. Notice the waveform you measured.
Let's determine whether C3 is open or R3 is shorted.
2. Measure the resistance of R3 (TP6 to TP7).

text: Check your resistance measurement across R3 (TP7 to TP1). You should measure approximately 10 kW, indicating R3 is good. This leaves C3 open as the probable fault.
3. Remove the multimeter and place S3 on PC130-14B to In (Right). The computer will now replace C3. rnal program = SCAN FTR 0 C3 00..................................
Is circuit C operating normally? normally?
Ensure you are measuring across C3 (TP7 to TP1). Notice that the waveform represents the charge and discharge voltage. This is correct for an input frequency of 100 Hz.
Congratulations, you have correctly determined and verified the fault.
